p0.issue: H2 success metrics referenced Appointment Confirmation Rate and Human Handoff Rate, but neither was in the H1 instrumentation scope. H2 Initiative 1 (Vertical Templates) requires Appointment Confirmation Rate ≥50%; H2 Initiative 2 (CRM Data Capture) requires Human Handoff Rate to drop ≥20%. Both metrics were in the framework's metric tree but absent from the six-metric first dashboard that H1 committed to instrumenting. At H2 evaluation time, both success metrics would have been unmeasurable.
p0.resolution: Fixed in 03-roadmap.json: H1 Initiative 1 success metric expanded to explicitly require instrumentation of Appointment Confirmation Rate (claim f10) and Human Handoff Rate (claim f11) alongside the original six dashboard metrics. Two new baseline claims (f10, f11) added to the roadmap.

p0.issue: H1 Initiative 2 success metric contained '≥60%' as a hard activation rate target with no claim record and no grounding. The notes acknowledged the number was 'directional' but directional targets in success metrics are still quantitative commitments. No industry benchmark, internal data, or competitive reference was cited to support 60% as the threshold. A target that is acknowledged to be made up in the same document that sets it is not a success metric — it is a placeholder.
p0.resolution: Fixed in 03-roadmap.json: success metric rewritten as '≥10 percentage points above the H1-measured baseline, with a minimum absolute floor of 50%.' The 50% floor is now backed by claim r05 (no-code SaaS category benchmark, marked estimate). The absolute target is relative to measured baseline rather than an invented absolute.

p0.issue: The Step 5 sensitivity table sensitized on tier mix (the variable BotConversa controls) but held the operational cost base constant at R$50,000/month — the most uncertain variable in the entire model, recorded as a null estimate (claim m01). This produced a single break-even number (234 accounts) that appears precise but is entirely dependent on an unverified cost assumption. If actual costs are R$75K/month the break-even is 350 accounts; at R$100K/month it is 467 accounts — a 2x spread that changes the viability story from 'achievable' to 'requires significant growth.' A sensitivity table that doesn't sensitize on its most uncertain variable is reverse-engineering the answer.
p0.resolution: Fixed in 05-monetization.json: two cost-sensitivity scenarios added (S5 at R$75K/month, S6 at R$100K/month) both at S3 tier mix. breakEven field updated to present the range (234/350/467 accounts) rather than a single number. The cost-sensitive nature of the break-even is now explicit.

p0.issue: H1 listed 'Instrument the North Star Dashboard' as Initiative 1 and 'Activation Redesign + Escape Hatch' as Initiative 2, implying Initiative 1 could proceed independently. But the North Star (ARR) requires conversations to reach 'defined terminal states' — and those terminal states don't exist as an enforced schema requirement until Initiative 2 (escape hatch enforcement at publish time) ships. Instrumenting ARR before terminal states are defined produces data that counts user abandonment as resolution — gaming risk #1 from the framework, introduced by the framework's own implementation plan.
p0.resolution: Fixed in 03-roadmap.json: H1 Initiative 1 success metric now contains an explicit ORDERING CONSTRAINT — 'ARR instrumentation must not begin until H1 Initiative 2 (Escape Hatch) has defined and enforced terminal-state events on all flows.' Notes updated to reflect Initiative 2 as a prerequisite for Initiative 1 to produce valid ARR data.

p0.issue: Step 5 (Monetization) introduced '15-day free trial replaces the current try-before-pay friction' as part of the recommended model. This is a concrete operational change — it affects acquisition mechanics, billing configuration, and the activation timeline. But it appeared in no roadmap initiative (Step 3). It had no owner, no success metric, and no H1/H2/H3 horizon assignment. A recommendation with no owner does not get implemented.
p0.resolution: Fixed in 03-roadmap.json: the 15-day trial change is explicitly added to H1 Initiative 2 (Activation Redesign) scope — 'Trial mechanics: 15-day free trial (extended from current) is the activation vehicle for this redesign — trial length change is owned by this initiative.' It now has a home, an owner (Product), and a horizon (H1).

p0.issue: H3 Initiative 1 (Vertical Performance Benchmarks) problem statement contained: 'BotConversa will by H3 have structured booking and conversation data across thousands of beauty salons, clinics, and pet shops.' 'Thousands' is a quantitative value in narrative prose with no claim record — a direct violation of the hard rule 'Never write a quantitative value into narrative text without a claim record.' Worse, the current account count (claim f06) is null. If BotConversa has 300–500 accounts today and grows modestly, 'thousands' may not be true by H3, which would invalidate the benchmark feature's entire statistical premise.
p0.resolution: Fixed in 03-roadmap.json: 'thousands' removed and replaced with 'a peer group large enough to generate statistically meaningful benchmarks per vertical and city (minimum peer-group size to be defined at H2 review checkpoint — see claim r06).' Claim r06 added as a placeholder for the statistical minimum, to be determined when account distribution data (claim f09) is available.

p1.issue: H2 success metric targets are unsupported by benchmarks: '≥3 active flows per account' (H2 Init 1), '≥50% Appointment Confirmation Rate' (H2 Init 1), '≥40% of accounts with ≥1 CRM field' (H2 Init 2), '≥20% relative reduction in Human Handoff Rate' (H2 Init 2). All four are directional estimates set without industry benchmarks or BotConversa-specific data. They are better than no targets, but they carry false precision. All four must be revisited and justified with H1 baseline data before H2 investment is committed.
p1.recommendation: At the H1/H2 boundary review, replace all four targets with values grounded in the H1 measurements. Document the revision rationale. Do not carry forward unsupported targets into H2 OKRs.

p1.issue: Claim r02's source field incorrectly references 'claim f01' as the basis for the Appointment Confirmation Rate baseline. f01 is the ARR baseline, not the Appointment Confirmation Rate baseline. The correct reference is f10 (added during P0-A fix). This is a cross-reference error that would produce confusion during the data-request workflow.
p1.recommendation: Update r02 source to reference f10 instead of f01. Minor fix, but the ledger cross-references are the integrity layer of this pipeline — they should be correct.

p1.issue: SocialHub pricing (claim c10, R$197/month) is marked 'estimate' because the pricing page was blocked by bot protection and could not be directly verified. However, the Step 5 sensitivity table S1 notes reference 'SocialHub's estimated entry price (claim c10)' in a competitive positioning argument. Using an unverified competitor price as a competitive anchor creates a weak argument — if SocialHub's actual entry price is R$149 or R$249, the positioning claim inverts.
p1.recommendation: Retry the SocialHub pricing page fetch in a future session or have a team member confirm directly. Until confirmed, the S1 competitive positioning note should be qualified: 'below SocialHub's reported entry price, unverified (claim c10).'

p1.issue: ManyChat pricing (claims c01, c01b) was sourced from third-party blog articles because manychat.com/pricing returned 403. Third-party pricing articles can be 6–12 months stale, especially since ManyChat announced a pricing transition for Brazil in 2026. The Essential plan at $14/month and Pro plan at $29/month may not reflect current Brazilian pricing when it launches.
p1.recommendation: Re-verify ManyChat pricing once Brazil-specific pricing goes live (announced for 'later in 2026'). Flag in any synthesis text that ManyChat Brazil pricing is in transition and current USD prices are a proxy.

p1.issue: The typing error 'Inflating the denominator denominator' appears in 02-framework.json, gamingRisks[3]. Cosmetic, but it will render verbatim in the DOCX appendix.
p1.recommendation: Fix the duplicate word in 02-framework.json gamingRisks[3] before rendering.

p1.issue: The H3 gating condition in the roadmap objective reads 'Logo Churn Rate dropping to ≤X% and ARR reaching ≥Y%' with literal X and Y placeholders — these are supposed to be filled in from H1 baselines, but the document renders them as symbolic variables, which looks incomplete. The intent is correct but the presentation signals an unfinished document.
p1.recommendation: At H1 completion, replace X and Y with the actual measured baselines plus target deltas. Until then, note explicitly in the H3 objective that these are placeholders pending H1 measurement — the current text already implies this but the literal X/Y creates an unfinished appearance.
